title: Ops leanpath: capacity-to-price mapping and headcount floorplan (prototype)
content:
Purpose:
This prototype maps capacity (GPU pool + reserved slots + burst) to marginal pricing bands and a corresponding minimal headcount floorplan for operations-critical teams. Intended as a rapid experiment for the Q1 planning cycle to inform runway and pricing trigger rules. Not final — intended to be an input to the Feb planning offsite.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We model three capacity states (Constrained, Normal, Ample) and three pricing bands (Low, Mid, High). Each capacity state implies a recommended set of hiring deferrals, contract renewals, and burst capacity retention. At current run-rate, moving from Mid->High pricing reduces demand by ~12% (elasticity assumption) and allows us to defer 6 FTEs across engineering + SRE in the next 6 months while preserving customer SLAs with a 15% increase in burst usage. If pricing remains in the Low band, we recommend a progressive hiring schedule to bring product and research hires back online in Q3.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Forecast horizon: 12 months from 2026-03-01.
- Revenue baseline: $27.4M ARR growing to $36.1M under base-case demand.
- Token-unit price sensitivity: price increase of 10% -> demand fall of 6% (base elasticity = -0.6); 20% -> demand fall of 12% (elasticity approx -0.6 consistently).
- Capacity cost profile: Reserved capacity amortized @ $0.43 per token equivalent; burst GPU spot @ $0.78 per token equivalent average; private/on-prem marginal cost @ $0.35 per token equivalent (includes infra + ops).
- Hiring: average fully-burdened cost per HC = engineering $320k, SRE $300k, product $220k, sales/CS $210k, research $340k.
- Hiring lead time: 10 weeks for IC eng, 14 weeks for senior, 6 weeks for sales/CS.
- Buffer SLO: must maintain 99.5% request success and p95 latency target per route.

Scenario definitions:
- Constrained: sustained capacity shortage (reserved pools 20% below plan), burst increases 2x, expected churn risk up 3 pts. Pricing band = High (raise unit price by 20% to curb demand).
- Normal (base): capacity meets expected demand, burst <10% of requests, pricing band = Mid (flat pricing or small promo windows).
- Ample: sustained headroom (reserved pools >=120% of expected), burst usage <5%, pricing band = Low (promotional pricing to grow market share).

Capacity-to-price mapping (summary table):
Mode,Reserved utilization %,Burst as % of traffic,Price band,Recommended unit price delta
Constrained, 80, 30, High, +20%
Normal, 100, 8, Mid, 0%
Ample, 120, 3, Low, -10%

Headcount floorplan (minimal ops-critical coverage by scenario) — FTE counts (6m rolling):
Role,Constrained,Normal,Ample
Core Serving Eng, 18, 24, 28
SRE/Infra, 6, 9, 11
Platform/Build, 4, 6, 8
Product (ops-facing), 2, 4, 6
Solutions & PS, 3, 4, 6
Sales/CS (quota-support), 18, 22, 28
Research/Applied, 1, 4, 6
Total (ops + customer-facing), 52, 73, 93

Hiring phasing (quarterly plan, example for Normal case):
Q2-2026: +6 eng (4 backend, 2 infra), +2 SRE, +3 sales/CS
Q3-2026: +8 eng (mix), +2 product, +4 sales/CS, +1 research
Q4-2026: +4 eng, +1 SRE, +2 solutions

Unit economics sensitivity (simplified):
Inputs: baseline tokens/month = 9.8B, baseline price per 1k tokens = $0.90 (hosted mix), baseline variable cost per 1k tokens = $0.42 (weighted reserved+burst mix).
Scenarios:
- 0% price change (Mid): revenue/month = 9.8B/1k * $0.90 = $8.82M; gross margin = (0.90-0.42)/0.90 = 53.3%
- +10% price: price = $0.99, demand drop -6% -> tokens = 9.212B, revenue = 9.212B/1k * $0.99 = $9.12M; variable cost effect reduced in proportion to tokens; net margin increases modestly.
- +20% price: price = $1.08, demand -12% -> tokens = 8.624B, revenue = 8.624B/1k * $1.08 = $9.32M; variable costs fall and margin improves; but product adoption risk increases.
Note: elasticities above are illustrative and should be validated via A/B price tests on a subset of non-enterprise customers.

Cash and runway sensitivity table (6-month view):
Line,Constrained,Normal,Ample
Revenue delta vs baseline, -11%, 0%, +9%
Opex (headcount + infra) delta vs baseline, -9%, 0%, +14%
Net burn delta vs baseline, +12%, 0%, -25%

Recommended pricing triggers (operational rules):
- Trigger A (capacity). If reserved utilization >95% for 10 consecutive days, move pricing -> +10% for variable-plan cohorts and enable stricter rate limits for new signups.
- Trigger B (SLO drift). If p95 latency increases beyond 1.4x target on two consecutive measurement windows, route >=20% of traffic to private/dedicated variants and increase price on hosted tier for non-committed customers.
- Trigger C (demand shock). If day-over-day token consumption drops >18% after a price increase, pause further price increases and activate growth promotions to test elasticity.

Operational playbook (condensed):
Short-term (0-3 months):
- Execute a small A/B price experiment on lower-tier hosted customers (target 5% of live tokens) to validate -0.6 elasticity assumption. Monitor retention at 30/60 days.
- Freeze non-essential hiring except critical SRE/serving eng (2 hires) until we have A/B results.
- Negotiate a 30-day flexible addendum with our primary burst GPU vendor to reduce spot exposure if constrained scenario manifests.

Medium-term (3-9 months):
- If price experiment supports elasticity model, roll a +10% price on variable plans and re-run unit-econ snapshot.
- If capacity remains constrained, prioritize automation projects that reduce token cost per request (KV cache improvements, batching improvements, compaction).

Long-term (9-12 months):
- Re-evaluate headcount floorplans and convert deferred IC hiring into targeted senior hires to keep productivity.
- Consider hybrid regional pricing where APAC regions see differentiated bands due to cost differences.

Open questions and risks:
- Model sensitivity to elasticity: default -0.6 assumed; if true elasticity is closer to -1.0, price increases will be more damaging to revenue. We must instrument customer cohorts before broad rollouts.
- Competitive response: large competitor discounting in Q2 could nullify our price experiment. Contingency: build rapid promo pipeline and partner credit offering.
- Contract exposure: some large enterprise customers on committed plans will not be able to be repriced quickly; need a mapping of top 25 accounts and exposure impact.

Next steps (owners & short timeline):
- Finance (Asha): finalize the experiment cohort and expected KPIs by 2026-03-10.
- Revenue Ops (Marcus): produce contract exposure report for top 25 accounts by 2026-03-14.
- Eng (Diego): create infra dashboard for reserved utilization + burst run-rate; ETA 2026-03-07.
- Product (Priya): prepare customer comms variants for +10% pricing (two tones) by 2026-03-12.

Document history and provenance: created as an ops-finance cross-functional prototype for the Feb planning offsite. This file intentionally mixes narrative with spreadsheet-like tables for rapid review.

Comments: please annotate with inline comments in Confluence-9876 if you have concerns about elasticity or the headcount phasing. This will be versioned after the offsite.
